RWA.note: The article says nothing on government e-procurement.

facts.fact: The National Bank of Rwanda governor said the central bank runs the eKash instant payment system as the national switch, and mandated that all person-to-person transactions take place on it.

The article says Rwanda is part of COMESA, which has its own regional payment system, the COMESA Clearing House, and that the central bank agreed to route intra-EAC payments through the regional EAC payment system and payments outside the EAC through PAPSS.

RWA.note: The article states a fee cap on eKash but no consumer-protection rules, complaints body or enforcement.

facts.fact: The National Bank of Rwanda launched a pilot that integrates eKash with Tanzania's Instant Payment System (TIPS), according to the article.
The article says Rwanda is part of COMESA, which has its own regional payment system, the COMESA Clearing House.

RWA.note: The article says nothing on government payments to people.

facts.fact: The National Bank of Rwanda governor said the central bank ended mobile money providers' bilateral relationships with banks and microfinance institutions and mandated that all person-to-person transactions take place on eKash.

RWA.note: The 92% account figure is stated by the governor with no survey named.

facts.fact: The article says the central bank eliminated mobile money providers' bilateral relationships with banks and microfinance institutions, so that all person-to-person transactions run on eKash.
The governor described eKash as the national switch, with transactions rising from 140,000 to 1 million a month between August and September 2026 and fees on transfers capped at 20 Rwandan francs.

RWA.note: The article says nothing on tax or fee payment.
